title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 6
paragraphs: The Athenians had crossed over to Salamis as follows. As long as they were expecting an army to come from the Peloponnese to help them, they remained in Attica; but the Peloponnesians acted very slowly and with great delay, while the invader was said to be already in Boeotia, so they removed everything out of danger and crossed over to Salamis themselves. At the same time they sent envoys to Lacedaemon to reproach the Lacedaemonians for having permitted the barbarian to invade Attica and for having failed to join them in going to Boeotia to meet him, and also to remind them how many things the Persian had promised to give the Athenians if they changed sides — telling the envoys to warn them that, if they did not help the Athenians, the Athenians would find some shelter for themselves.
